topic: Neural Networks: The Art of Learning from Mistakes (Intuitive Backpropagation)
target_audience: Beginner Computer Science Students / Tech Enthusiasts

sections.title: The Goal: Teaching 'Robo-Chef'
lecture_lines: Meet Robo-Chef, our apprentice learning to recognize food.
It sees a snail but shouts "Delicious Bread!"
The Disappointment Meter measures this massive 90% error.
animations: Display a character 'Robo-Chef' (#ADD8E6) in the center of the screen.
Robo-Chef looks at a snail photo (#FFFFFF) and a speech bubble appears: 'Delicious Bread!' (#FF6347).
A vertical bar 'Disappointment Meter' (#FF0000) appears on the right and fills up to 90%.

sections.title: Prerequisite: The Anatomy of a Neuron
lecture_lines: Neurons use "Volume Knobs" called weights for signals.
"Sensitivity Switches" or biases decide when to fire.
Turning knobs changes how the network perceives the world.
animations: Display a circle representing a 'Neuron' (#FFFFFF) with three input wires coming from the left.
Place 'Volume Knobs' (Weights, #FFD700) on each wire and a 'Sensitivity Switch' (Bias, #00FF00) inside the neuron.
Turn the 'Slime' knob (#ADFF2F) up; a light labeled 'Snail' (#FFFFE0) on the output side glows brightly.

sections.title: The Forward Pass: Making a Guess
lecture_lines: Signals flow forward, multiplying by weights at each step.
The "Threshold Gate" decides which information passes through.
Finally, the network outputs its best guess.
animations: Show a neural network structure; glowing pulses of light (#FFFF00) travel from left to right.
A 'Threshold Gate' icon (#00FFFF) flashes inside each neuron as pulses pass through.
At the final layer, the 'Bread' light (#F5DEB3) flashes weakly while the 'Snail' light remains dark.

sections.title: The Loss Function: Measuring the Gap
lecture_lines: Error is a physical distance in the Loss Valley.
Being wrong means being stuck high on a mountain.
We must find the path to the valley floor.
animations: Draw a jagged brown mountain range 'Loss Valley' (#8B4513) with a white ball (#FFFFFF) high on a peak.
Highlight the ball as 'Current State' and show its height relative to the valley floor.
A red arrow (#FF0000) points the path down from the peak to the green 'Valley of Correctness' (#00FF00).

sections.title: Intuitive Backpropagation: The Blame Game
lecture_lines: We look backward from the error to the knobs.
Which specific knob contributed most to the mistake?
This "Blame Game" is the essence of backpropagation.
Red arrows point back, assigning responsibility to each neuron.
We calculate the gradient: the direction of highest error.
animations: Show the neural network from Section 3 with the 'Snail' output light highlighted with a red glow (#FF0000).
A red arrow (#FF0000) points backward from the output to the previous layer's knobs.
The 'Slime' knob is highlighted; text 'Turn Me Down!' (#FF6347) appears above it.
Similar red arrows point to other knobs, labeled with the word 'Gradient' (#FF4500).
Text 'Assigning Blame (Chain Rule)' appears in light blue (#87CEEB) at the bottom.

sections.title: Gradient Descent: The Tiny Step
lecture_lines: We use the calculated blame to adjust the knobs.
A tiny wrench nudges each weight toward the truth.
The "Learning Rate" determines the size of our step.
Too big a step, and we overshoot the valley.
Just right, and we descend safely toward zero error.
animations: Return to the white ball (#FFFFFF) on the brown mountain (#8B4513) from Section 4.
A 'Tiny Wrench' (#C0C0C0) icon appears and nudges the ball slightly downhill.
Simultaneously, show the 'Slime' knob from Section 5 turning slightly counter-clockwise.
The label 'Learning Rate' (#00BFFF) appears next to the wrench to indicate the step size.
The ball settles a bit lower on the slope; text 'Loss Decreased' (#32CD32) appears.

sections.title: The Iterative Loop: Practice Makes Perfect
lecture_lines: Learning is repeating "Guess, Blame, and Adjust" cycles.
Watch as the knobs settle into their perfect positions.
Now, Robo-Chef identifies the snail with zero disappointment.
animations: Rapidly cycle snail/croissant images on the left while knobs (weights) in the center spin and settle.
The white ball (#FFFFFF) reaches the green 'Valley of Correctness' (#00FF00) at the bottom.
A final snail image is shown; Robo-Chef says 'Snail!' (#00FF00) and the 'Disappointment Meter' stays empty.
